text: hey everybody what do I mean when I say that engaging the Bible is a process of negotiation starts from the observation that texts don't have any inherent
meaning all of the meaning is generated within the mind of a hearer a viewer or a reader based on their understanding of
and their experiences with the different agreements that have been reached regarding relationships between shapes on a surface and between certain sounds
and then between certain sounds and certain semantic content and those relationships can be phenomenally complex and nuanced and they will differ
from time to time from place to place and from person to person and so already just because the Bible is a text we must negotiate with it by rifling through
potential meanings to settle on the meanings that we believe are intended and that happens almost instantaneously
and subconsciously so we're not really aware of it but then if we engage or deploy the Bible authoritatively or
socially we bring in social dynamics any traditional readings that may be authoritative we bring in feel logical
correctness we bring in the presupposition of univocality or the notion that the Bible speaks with one single and consistent unified voice and
that's not supported by any of the data but all of that combines to help us to prioritize certain texts in their interpretation and then to marginalize
or reinterpret other texts in order to allow those prioritized texts to be centered and this helps us to negotiate
a meaning that will make the text most meaningful or most useful to us
